batches.strategy: merge reliability and one-click release into the existing v1.7 ports page
equivalentImplementation: the bounded synchronous scan replaces separate scan status, enrichment and cancellation commands while preserving durable errors and native fallback
recommended or full scan scope and startup monitoring preferences are persisted by the backend
safe user-owned listeners retain one-click release, and Markdown or JSON reports are redacted before export

batches.strategy: keep existing runtime cards and actions; perform plan validation transparently

verified switch receipts can be listed and restored once without exposing plan or token controls
Maven and Gradle accept validated release versions, and strong verification reports export as redacted Markdown or JSON

batches.strategy: add useful actions to existing v1.7 cleanup sections without a second execution screen

the frontend submits only an opaque plan ID; the backend consumes the immutable stored plan once and rejects reuse or expiry
recycle-bin preview, execution, verified rescan and rollback guidance remain durable in the existing cleanup result area

batches.strategy: extend the existing profile list and preserve one-confirmation apply and history restore behavior

history restore creates and consumes an internal fingerprint-bound single-use plan without exposing token UX
copy, rename, import picker and durable result handling remain inside the v1.7 profile panel

batches.strategy: replace the legacy direct repair internally while retaining its existing button and result panel

success and failure remain visible in the existing doctor result panel

batches.strategy: wire bounded application search and single-confirmation execution into the existing file-association controls

registry backups preserve exact raw values for rollback and all actions render durable page results
